name: Nutrition Foundations
description: Understand basic nutrients, balanced meals, and how food impacts energy, focus, and mood.

name: Food Quality Awareness
description: Recognize whole vs ultra-processed foods, added sugar/salt, and simple indicators of food quality.

name: Reading Food Labels (Age-Appropriate)
description: Interpret simple nutrition labels/ingredients to identify healthier options (e.g., sugar, fiber, additives).

name: Healthy Plate & Portion Sense
description: Build balanced plates and develop portion awareness using age-appropriate guidance.

name: Hydration & Body Signals
description: Recognize thirst/body cues and build hydration habits that support attention and wellbeing.

name: Mindful Eating & Hunger Cues
description: Notice hunger/fullness cues, eat with awareness, and reduce distracted eating habits.

name: Food Safety & Hygiene
description: Practice safe food handling basics and hygiene routines that prevent illness.

name: Sleep Hygiene
description: Understand and practice healthy sleep routines; recognize how sleep affects learning and mood.

name: Daily Movement Habits
description: Practice regular movement and stretching; understand its role in focus, mood, and health.

name: Posture & Ergonomics
description: Use healthy posture and study setup habits to reduce fatigue and support concentration.

name: Hygiene & Self-Care Routines
description: Practice age-appropriate hygiene and self-care routines that support health and confidence.

name: Safety Awareness
description: Learn safe behaviors and basic precautions in school, home, and activity settings.

name: Healthy Environment Habits
description: Maintain clean, organized learning spaces and understand basic environmental health impacts (air, cleanliness).

name: Wellbeing Tracking & Reflection
description: Track simple routines (sleep, food, water, movement) and reflect on effects on performance and mood.

name: Health Literacy Basics
description: Understand basic concepts like germs, immunity, prevention habits in an educational (non-medical) way.

name: Food Culture & Balanced Choices
description: Understand cultural foods and make balanced choices without stigma; respect diversity in diet.

name: Emotion Identification
description: Identify and name emotions in self and others with age-appropriate vocabulary.

name: Self-Regulation
description: Use strategies to calm down, pause, and manage impulses during challenges.

name: Stress Awareness
description: Recognize signs of stress and understand healthy responses and support-seeking.

name: Resilience & Growth Mindset
description: Persist through setbacks, learn from mistakes, and maintain constructive self-talk.

name: Empathy & Perspective
description: Understand others’ feelings and perspectives; respond with care and respect.

name: Emotional Reflection
description: Reflect on feelings, choices, and consequences to improve future decisions.

name: Coping Strategies
description: Develop a toolkit of coping strategies (breathing, journaling, reframing, asking for help).

name: Self-Awareness & Values
description: Identify personal strengths, triggers, and values that guide behavior and decisions.

name: Conflict Calmness
description: Respond calmly in conflicts; de-escalate and choose respectful solutions.

name: Wellbeing Routines (Non-Clinical)
description: Practice wellbeing routines (check-ins, mindful pauses) as educational supports for mental balance.

name: Reading Comprehension
description: Understand texts and demonstrate comprehension through summaries, questions, and evidence.

name: Reasoning & Justification
description: Explain why/how; justify answers using logic and evidence.

name: Problem Solving
description: Solve multi-step problems by selecting strategies, checking solutions, and refining approaches.

name: Critical Thinking
description: Evaluate claims, compare sources, identify assumptions, and draw evidence-based conclusions.

name: Inquiry & Investigation
description: Ask questions, investigate, collect observations/data, and form conclusions.

name: Scientific Method & Experimentation
description: Form hypotheses, design simple experiments, observe, record results, and interpret outcomes.

name: Data Literacy & Evidence Use
description: Read charts/tables, interpret data, and use evidence to support conclusions.

name: Systems Thinking (Real World)
description: Understand systems with inputs/outputs/feedback; identify cause-effect relationships in real contexts.

name: Applied Learning (Real Context)
description: Apply learning to real-life scenarios, case studies, and practical examples (finance, health, environment, daily life).

name: Modeling & Simulation Thinking
description: Use models (drawings, equations, simple simulations) to represent and predict real-world behavior.

name: Engineering Design & Prototyping
description: Define problems, generate solutions, prototype, test, and iterate using constraints.

name: Interdisciplinary Application
description: Connect concepts across subjects (science + math + society) to solve complex real problems.

name: Conceptual Understanding
description: Build deep understanding of concepts; connect ideas across topics beyond memorization.

name: Metacognition (How to Learn)
description: Plan, monitor, and reflect on learning strategies and progress.

name: Creativity in Thinking
description: Generate ideas, explore alternatives, and create novel solutions within learning tasks.

name: Knowledge Organization
description: Organize information using notes, mind maps, summaries, and structured representations.
